oil.summary: Crude sold off sharply Wednesday, with Brent down 2.80% to $86.07 and WTI off 1.40% to $81.17, extending a steep weekly slide of roughly 6% from levels that had been elevated by Hormuz closure fears. The catalyst for today's move was diplomatic: Iran-Oman talks on joint Strait of Hormuz management revived hopes that the chokepoint could reopen, pulling risk premium out of flat price. RBOB gasoline cratered 9.88% on the day — a standout move suggesting physical tightness is easing. Bearish inventory data reinforced the selloff; API reported a 4.2 million barrel crude build for the week ending August 21, even as the SPR approaches operational minimums. Countervailing supply risks remain — Ukraine struck Russia's Afipsky refinery and Rystad cut Russia's 2026 output forecast to 8.95 mb/d — but diplomacy dominated sentiment today.
drivers: Iran-Oman Hormuz diplomacy eased closure premium, pressuring Brent and WTI lower on the session
API crude inventory build of 4.2 mb and surging Iraqi export loadings added bearish supply-side pressure
Ukraine drone strikes on Russian refinery infrastructure and Canada oil sands output cuts introduce offsetting supply-risk tail

gas.summary: Henry Hub firmed 3.79% to $2.875/MMBtu, extending a monthly gain of 8%, while European TTF eased 2.57% to €64.88/MWh — likely tracking the modest Hormuz diplomatic optimism seen in crude — though TTF remains up over 12% on the month. The fundamental backdrop stays tight: Qatar has lost an estimated $24 billion as LNG exports via the Strait of Hormuz have collapsed 96% since the Iran war began, removing a major swing supplier from Atlantic Basin markets. Norway's Troll Phase 3 Stage 2 start-up accelerates 55 bcm of reserves but is described as buying Europe time rather than adding new net supply. UK energy bills are set to hit a three-year high this winter, reflecting the structural tightness in European gas driven by the Iran conflict.
drivers: Qatar LNG exports down 96% since Hormuz disruption began, removing critical global LNG swing supply
Norway Troll Phase 3 Stage 2 online but categorized as acceleration of existing reserves, not incremental new supply
UK regulator raising energy price caps ahead of winter on sustained elevated gas prices, signaling demand-side stress

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs edged up 0.39% to $79.87, posting a solid 2.40% weekly and 2.42% monthly gain, consistent with elevated TTF gas prices feeding through to higher power generation costs and supporting carbon demand. Headline flow in the power and carbon space was light on price-specific catalysts today, but two thematic stories stand out: uranium futures briefly surpassed $100/lb recently on tightening supplies and accelerating nuclear demand, and a separate report notes major oil companies are directing billions toward nuclear fusion development. Secretary Rubio's statement that there will be no further immediate strikes on Iran may reduce near-term geopolitical risk premia marginally, though sanctions targeting Iranian oil exports continue to shape the broader energy complex.
drivers: EUA prices grinding higher, supported by elevated TTF gas costs raising thermal power generation expense
Uranium spot briefly above $100/lb and major oil-company fusion investment signal accelerating structural shift toward nuclear
Rubio 'no further Iran strikes for now' comment offers modest geopolitical de-escalation signal, though Iran oil sanctions remain in force
